name: Corneal wing cell
blurb: A living cell from the middle of the clear skin of the eye: a many-sided cell with a round nucleus, riveted to its neighbours at the sides, in a stack five to seven cells deep.
note: Model: a wing cell from the middle of the human corneal epithelium, cut in half. The flat surface cell and the tall basal cell are drawn as cells of their own. Measured in human eyes: the width of a wing cell (confocal), the thickness of the epithelium, the size and thickness of the surface cell, the height of the basal cell, and a wing-cell height calculated from a measured layer thickness, that the cells carry desmosomes at their sides and are rich in keratin bundles. Illustrative: this cell's sides, the nucleus, the mitochondria, the Golgi, the number of desmosomes and keratin bundles, and the colours. The neighbours show faintly. Not drawn: microvilli and surface folds, tight junctions, hemidesmosomes, nerve endings.

epithelium_thickness.note: central cornea; Sridhar gives about 50 µm and Wikipedia (wikipedia_ce) gives approximately 50 to 52 µm, which is the range used; 5 to 7 cell layers centrally

surface_cell_width.note: the surface cell, not drawn here; the midpoint of the range given

surface_cell_thickness.note: the surface cell, not drawn here; Sridhar gives 2 to 6 µm, and 4 µm is the midpoint of that range (calculated)

basal_cell_height.calc: a basal cell is 40% of the thickness (ghafar2021): 0.4 x 50 µm = 20 µm, the same as the 20 µm given directly
basal_cell_height.note: the basal cell, not drawn here; confocal microscopy of the central cornea gives a thinner basal layer, 12.7 ± 3.8 µm (mathews2015), against about 20 µm in histology

width.note: central-cornea wing (suprabasal) cell diameter by in vivo confocal microscopy, 21.5 ± 1.3 µm (mean ± SD, three subjects; mathews2015 Table 1)

height.calc: calculated from a measured value: the central-cornea wing layer is 18.3 ± 5.0 µm thick (mathews2015, confocal), divided by 2 to 3 wing layers (sridhar2018), taken as 2.5, gives 7.3 µm. Cross-check from histology: (50 µm total - about 4 µm surface cell - about 20 µm basal cell) / 2.5 wing layers is about 10 µm per wing cell (sridhar2018, ghafar2021). The range is about 7 to 10 µm; 7.3 µm, the confocal figure, is drawn

basement_membrane.note: the sheet under the basal cells

size_um.note: illustrative: no source opened gives a nucleus size; the nuclei of the surface cells are flat (wikipedia_ce); a wing nucleus is drawn between flat and round, as an illustration

nucleus.position_note: illustrative: no opened source gives the nucleus position

special.note: Wing cells are rich in keratin filament bundles (tonofilaments) (measured fact, not counted). 14 bundles are drawn, thick enough to see; their number and paths are illustrative.
Desmosomes lie along the sides of all the epithelial cells (measured fact, not counted). 120 are drawn on the cell's surface, an illustrative number.

cut: The cell is cut in half through its middle: a round nucleus with its nucleolus in the centre, bundles of keratin filaments running from side to side to the desmosomes on the sides, and a few small mitochondria and a Golgi apparatus. The cells beside it show faintly.

colours.convention: Cell membrane pale; the inside dark; keratin bundles straw yellow; desmosomes brown; nucleus violet; mitochondria orange. All colours are a code; none is the real colour of the cell, which is clear and colourless.

cytosol.name: Cytosol
cytosol.about: The watery inside of the cell, crowded with proteins.

keratin.name: Keratin filaments
keratin.about: Bundles of keratin filaments run through a wing cell and end at its desmosomes, so that the stack of cells takes a rub or a blink as one sheet.

about: The cornea's outer skin is about 50 µm thick and five to seven cells deep. It has three kinds of cell: flat surface cells on top (40 to 60 µm across, 2 to 6 µm thick), many-sided wing cells in the middle, and tall basal cells on the bottom (about 20 µm), which are the only ones that divide. This picture shows one wing cell, {drawn.cellVolume} µm³ as drawn. The surface cell, a much wider and thinner plate, and the basal cell, a taller column set on the basement membrane, are drawn as cells of their own.

The cells are alive and keep their nuclei (the nucleus drawn is {drawn.nuclei} of {drawn.nucleiWanted}). Unlike skin, the surface is not a layer of dead scales. Keratin bundles and {drawn.desmosomes} desmosomes tie the cells together; surface cells in life also seal their sides with tight junctions, and basal cells grip the basement membrane with hemidesmosomes. The hemidesmosomes are drawn with the basal cell; the tight junctions are not drawn.
A cell lasts only about a week to ten days: it is born at the bottom, moves up and is shed into the tears. The sizes of the nucleus and the small organelles are illustrative, not measured.

sridhar2018.cite: Sridhar MS (2018) Anatomy of cornea and ocular surface, Indian J Ophthalmol 66:190-194
sridhar2018.used_for: human corneal epithelium about 50 µm thick, 5-7 layers centrally; surface cells flat, 40-60 µm across and 2-6 µm thick; wing cells 2-3 layers; basal cells single layer, columnar, about 20 µm tall, joined to the basement membrane by hemidesmosomes; desmosomes along the lateral membranes of all cells; basement membrane 40-60 nm; cells live 7-10 days

ghafar2021.cite: Ghafar NA, Jalil NAA, Kamarudin TA (2021) Wound healing of the corneal epithelium: a review, Asian Biomed 15:199-212
ghafar2021.used_for: epithelium about 50 µm in humans, 5-7 layers; superficial layer 2-4 layers with microplicae and microvilli; lateral desmosomes, adherens and tight junctions; wing cells rich in tonofilaments; basal cells are the only dividing cells and make up 40% of the thickness; hemidesmosomes anchor basal cells

mathews2015.cite: Mathews S et al. (2015) In vivo confocal microscopic analysis of normal human anterior limbal stroma, Cornea 34:464-470
mathews2015.used_for: Table 1, in vivo confocal microscopy of three subjects, central cornea: wing (suprabasal) cells 21.5 ± 1.3 µm across, layer 18.3 ± 5.0 µm thick, 4078 ± 237 cells/mm²; basal cells 12.8 ± 0.7 µm across, layer 12.7 ± 3.8 µm thick, 6787 ± 274 cells/mm². Limbal wing cells 21.2 ± 1.2 µm, layer 27 ± 14.2 µm

wikipedia_ce.used_for: central thickness about 50 to 52 µm; superficial layers squamous with flattened nuclei; wing cells polyhedral; basal cells columnar; hemidesmosomes; constant mitosis
